## Summary  
The 2025 corn crop in Elmore County is completed. Yield estimate is **149 bu/acre** with an 80 % range of 118 to 178 bu/acre. The field shows a low‑NDVI zone in the southeast and soil pH below the optimal range.

## Crop health  
Peak NDVI was 0.86 and peak NDRE was 0.72 on 2025‑06‑27. Clear satellite images were available on 28 dates. The low zone covered 22.4 % of the field and had a mean NDVI of 0.769.

## Problem areas  
Low zone exists in the southeast. Soil pH values of 4.5 and 5.3 are below the optimal 6.0 to 6.5 range. Roanoke and Wehadkee soils are poorly drained. Water deficit is large.

## Weather  
Total rain was 24.8 in. Water balance was –5.3 in. Heat stress days were 4. Longest dry spell was 16 days. Summer heat averaged 92.6 °F versus a typical 90.8 °F, which lowered the estimate. Longest dry spell lasted 21.0 days versus a typical 16.2 days, which lowered the estimate. Summer rainfall was 12.6 in versus a typical 14.2 in, which lowered the estimate.

## Soil  
Roanoke silt loam (32.8 %) has pH 4.5 and is poorly drained. Wickham fine sandy loam (31.3 %) has pH 5.3 and is well drained. Augusta silt loam (31.2 %) has pH 5.3 and is somewhat poorly drained. Wehadkee silt loam (4.7 %) has pH 5.5 and is poorly drained. Field available water is 6.1 in.

## Yield outlook  
County‑level estimate is 149 bu/acre. 80 % confidence range is 118 to 178 bu/acre. Summer heat, longest dry spell, and reduced summer rainfall all lowered the estimate.

## What to check next  
- Apply lime to raise soil pH.  
- Improve drainage in poorly drained areas.  
- Plan supplemental irrigation for large water deficit.  
- Monitor the southeast low‑NDVI zone for future planting.
